stem: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 4:20?
What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 7:45?
explanation: Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |30 × 7 − 5.5 × 45| = |210 − 247.5| = 37.5°. This is less than 180°, so it is the smaller angle.

stem: At what time between 5 o'clock and 6 o'clock will the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock coincide?
explanation: At 5:00 the minute hand is 25 minute-spaces behind the hour hand. It gains 55 minute-spaces every 60 minutes, so it catches up in 25 × 60/55 = 300/11 = 27 3/11 minutes. The hands coincide at 27 3/11 minutes past 5.
shortcut: Hands coincide at 60H/11 minutes past H

stem: A clock gains 10 minutes for every hour of correct time. It is set right at 9:00 am. What is the correct time when this clock shows 4:00 pm on the same day?
explanation: In 60 minutes of correct time the clock moves 70 minutes. From 9:00 am to 4:00 pm the clock shows 420 minutes, which equals 420 × 60/70 = 360 minutes = 6 hours of correct time. Correct time = 9:00 am + 6 hours = 3:00 pm.

stem: 15 August 2023 was a Tuesday. What day of the week was 15 August 2024?
explanation: The period from 15 August 2023 to 15 August 2024 includes 29 February 2024, so it has 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 odd days. Tuesday + 2 days = Thursday.
shortcut: Same date next year: +1 day, or +2 if 29 Feb falls in between

stem: What day of the week was 26 January 1950?
explanation: Odd days up to 31 Dec 1949: 1600 years → 0; next 300 years → 1; 49 years (12 leap + 37 ordinary) → 24 + 37 = 61 → 5. Total = 6. Add 26 days of January 1950 → 5 odd days. 6 + 5 = 11 → 4 odd days. With 0 = Sunday, 4 = Thursday.

stem: Which of the following years will have exactly the same calendar as the year 2021?
explanation: 2021 is a non-leap year. Odd days: 2021 (1) + 2022 (1) + 2023 (1) + 2024 (2) + 2025 (1) + 2026 (1) = 7 ≡ 0. So 2027 starts on the same day as 2021, and being a non-leap year too, it has an identical calendar.
shortcut: Add odd days until the total is a multiple of 7, matching leap status

stem: How many times in a day (24 hours) are the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at right angles to each other?
explanation: In every 12 hours the hands are at right angles 22 times: twice in each hour, except that between 2 and 4 o'clock and between 8 and 10 o'clock one occurrence is shared (at 3:00 and 9:00), giving 24 − 2 = 22. In 24 hours this happens 2 × 22 = 44 times.
shortcut: Right angles: 44 per day; coincide: 22 per day
